'''Janelle Stelson''' (born 1960)<ref name="pnct23" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=May 21, 2012 |title=Getting to know you: Janelle Stelson |url=https://www.gettysburgtimes.com/news/local/getting-to-know-you-janelle-stelson/article_5664d737-2c3b-5693-ae78-a8fe44e9a1b1.html |access-date=July 16, 2026 |website=Gettysburg Times |language=en |quote=Hobbies: "I'm a Gemini. I tend to get interested in something and then get interested in something else."}}</ref> is an American former television [[news anchor]] and politician. She worked as a television journalist in [[Pennsylvania]] for more than three decades, including 26 years as an anchor at [[WGAL-TV]] in [[Lancaster, Pennsylvania|Lancaster]]. Stelson was the Democratic nominee for Pennsylvania's [[Pennsylvania's 10th congressional district|10th congressional district]] in [[2024 United States House of Representatives elections in Pennsylvania#District 10|2024]], narrowly losing to incumbent Republican [[Scott Perry]], and defeated him in the [[2026 United States House of Representatives elections in Pennsylvania#District 10|2026]] election.

== Early life and education ==
Stelson was born in [[Fairbanks, Alaska]], and raised in [[Seattle]] with three younger sisters.<ref name="pcskl">{{Cite web |last=Lyons |first=Kim |date=October 6, 2023 |title=Former WGAL anchor Janelle Stelson jumps into race for Congress |url=https://penncapital-star.com/campaigns-elections/former-wgal-anchor-janelle-stelson-jumps-into-race-for-congress/ |access-date=March 24, 2026 |website=Pennsylvania Capital-Star |language=en-US}}</ref> Her father was a [[state trooper]] and teacher, while her mother worked as a receptionist at [[Puget Sound Naval Shipyard]] in [[Bremerton, Washington]].<ref name="pcskl" /> 

She earned a Bachelor of Arts degree in politics and government from the [[University of Puget Sound]].<ref name="The Miami Herald from Miami, Florida">{{Cite web |date=July 15, 1989 |title=Janelle Stelson joins WPLG as general assignment reporter |url=https://www.newspapers.com/newspage/633413869/ |access-date=2025-10-10 |newspaper=[[The Miami Herald]] |via=Newspapers.com |language=en-US |page=73 |url-access=limited}}</ref> She also studied international politics and German at the Austro-American Institute in [[Vienna, Austria]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=November 22, 2011 |title=Janelle Stelson |url=https://www.wgal.com/article/janelle-stelson/6218406 |access-date=July 16, 2026 |website=[[WGAL-TV]] (Channel 8; NBC affiliate) |publisher=[[Hearst Television]] |language=en}}</ref>

==Broadcast journalism career==
After graduating from the University of Puget Sound, Stelson worked as a speechwriter at the [[Embassy of Egypt, Washington, D.C.|Embassy of Egypt]] in Washington, D.C.<ref name=":0" /> She later joined [[WHTM-TV]], the local [[List of American Broadcasting Company television affiliates|ABC affiliate]] in [[Harrisburg, Pennsylvania]], where she worked as a general assignment reporter and weather anchor for three years.<ref>{{cite news |title=WHTM's Janelle Stelson does reporting and weather |url=https://www.newspapers.com/newspage/1089339045/ |newspaper=[[The Patriot-News]] |date=September 27, 1987 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |page=80 |url-access=limited}}</ref> In 1985, she joined [[WPLG-TV]], the ABC affiliate in [[Miami, Florida]].<ref name="The Miami Herald from Miami, Florida" />

She later returned to Pennsylvania to join [[WHP-TV]], the [[CBS affiliate]] in Harrisburg, where she anchored the 6 pm and 11 pm newscasts.<ref>{{cite web |title=Stelson new WHP anchor |url=https://www.newspapers.com/newspage/554108131/ |newspaper=York Daily Record |date=28 December 1993 |via=Newspapers.com |page=27 |url-access=limited}}</ref> She also worked with [[WITF-FM]] radio, hosted a statewide public television program, and was a segment anchor on the national [[Public Broadcasting Service (PBS)|PBS]] series ''[[Computer Chronicles]]''.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Fox |first1=Barry |title=Janelle Stelson is back – sort of |url=https://www.newspapers.com/newspage/1091765129/ |newspaper=The Evening News |date=October 13, 1995 |via=Newspapers.com |page=35 |url-access=limited}}</ref>

In 1997, Stelson joined [[WGAL-TV]], the [[List of NBC television affiliates|NBC affiliate]] in [[Lancaster, Pennsylvania]],<ref>{{cite news |last1=Fox |first1=Barry |title=Janelle Stelson hired as anchor at WGAL |url=https://www.newspapers.com/newspage/1077840358/ |access-date=September 8, 2025 |newspaper=The Patriot-News |date=September 5, 1997 |via=Newspapers.com |page=47 |url-access=limited}}</ref> where she co-anchored the station's 4, 5:30, 10, and 11 pm evening newscasts.<ref>{{cite web |title=Janelle Stelson recalls the tragic shooting in an Amish school |url=https://www.wgal.com/article/janelle-stelson-recalls-the-tragic-shooting-in-an-amish-school/26913718 |website=WGAL |date=March 22, 2019}}</ref> During her time there, she reported from [[Kosovo]] while embedded with the [[Pennsylvania National Guard]] and covered the aftermath of the [[September 11 attacks]] at the [[World Trade Center (1973–2001)|World Trade Center]] in New York City.<ref>{{Cite web |last=White |first=Jaxon |date=September 14, 2023 |title=WGAL anchor Janelle Stelson leaving station, said to be considering run for Congress |url=https://lancasteronline.com/news/politics/wgal-anchor-janelle-stelson-leaving-station-said-to-be-considering-run-for-congress/article_8ae88956-534b-11ee-89ec-27a456691903.html |access-date=July 16, 2026 |website=Lancaster Online |language=en}}</ref> She won a [[Mid-Atlantic Emmy Awards|Mid-Atlantic Emmy Award]] in 2016<ref>{{cite web |url=https://natasmid-atlantic.org/awards/2016-emmy-recipients/ |title=2016 Emmy Recipients |date=September 24, 2023 |website=National Academy of Television Arts & Sciences Mid-Atlantic Chapter |access-date=April 27, 2026}}</ref> and 2023, including the latter for co-anchoring for a smaller market evening newscast.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://natasmid-atlantic.org/awards/2023-emmy-recipients/ |title=2023 Emmy Recipients |date=October 14, 2023 |website=National Academy of Television Arts & Sciences Mid-Atlantic Chapter |access-date=April 27, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.nbcphiladelphia.com/community/2023-mid-atlantic-regional-emmy-award-winners-announced/3669074/ |title= 2023 Mid-Atlantic Regional Emmy® Award Winners Announced |date=October 17, 2023 |website=[[WCAU]] |access-date=April 27, 2026}}</ref>

On September 14, 2023, Stelson announced near the end of "News 8 at 5:30" that she would be leaving WGAL after nearly 40 years as a journalist, including 26 years at the station. Her final newscast aired the following day.<ref name="pnct23">{{cite web |last1=Thompson |first1=Charles |title=Janelle Stelson leaving WGAL News 8 anchor desk |url=https://www.pennlive.com/news/2023/09/janelle-stelson-leaving-wgal-news-8s-anchor-desk.html |website=PennLive |date=September 14, 2023}}</ref>

== U.S. House of Representatives campaigns ==
=== 2024 election ===
{{Main|2024 United States House of Representatives elections in Pennsylvania#District 10|l1 = 2024 Pennsylvania's 10th congressional district election}}
In 2024, Stelson ran for Congress as a Democrat in [[Pennsylvania's 10th congressional district|Pennsylvania's 10th district]] on a centrist platform and defeated five other candidates in the Democratic primary.<ref name=":1" /> Ahead of the campaign, she changed her voter registration from [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] to [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] in February 2023. She said the [[Supreme Court of the United States|Supreme Court]]'s 2022 decision [[Overturning of Roe v. Wade|overturning ''Roe v. Wade'']] contributed to her decision, explaining that she had originally registered with the party of her parents. She also said that her career in broadcast journalism, which required political neutrality, had given her little reason to reconsider her party affiliation earlier.<ref name="pcskl" /> 

During the campaign, Stelson faced questions about her previous Republican registration and her residence outside the district. She said during a March primary debate that she would move into the district if she won the primary, but later said she would move after winning the general election.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Thompson |first=Charles |date=2024-06-13 |title=Janelle Stelson wants Pa. voters to commit before she moves. They might |url=https://www.pennlive.com/news/2024/06/janelle-stelson-wants-pa-voters-to-commit-first-she-might-get-away-with-it.html |access-date=2026-03-24 |website=pennlive |language=en}}</ref> She was also scrutinized for comments made on-air about a business in [[Belgium]] where patrons could dine and drink in the company of cats. After her co-anchor noted that the idea was popularized in Asian countries, she replied: "Of course, because they're making tacos out of them."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Argento |first=Mike |author-link=Mike Argento |title=Congressional hopeful and former WGAL anchor Janelle Stelson slammed for on-air Asian joke |url=https://www.ydr.com/story/news/2024/04/10/congressional-candidate-janelle-stelson-slammed-for-asian-joke/73277188007/ |access-date=2026-03-28 |website=York Daily Record |language=en-US}}</ref> She later apologized for the comment, saying it was inappropriate and had occurred during a career spanning thousands of hours of live television.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Thompson |first=Charles |date=2024-04-09 |title=Old racial 'joke' prompts criticism of central Pa. Democrat running for Congress |url=https://www.pennlive.com/elections/2024/04/old-racial-joke-prompts-criticism-of-central-pa-democrat-running-for-congress.html |access-date=2026-03-28 |website=pennlive |language=en}}</ref>

Stelson faced Republican incumbent [[Scott Perry]] in the [[2024 United States House of Representatives elections in Pennsylvania#District 10|general election]] and lost by about 5,000 votes.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Walters |first=Mark |title=Janelle Stelson moves into 10th Congressional District, changing voter registration |url=https://www.yorkdispatch.com/story/news/politics/elections/2025/08/20/janelle-stelson-moved-into-the-district-as-she-gears-up-for-pa-10-race/85735631007/ |access-date=2025-12-04 |website=York Dispatch |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Southard |first=Alexa |date=2024-11-08 |title=Janelle Stelson concedes in race for 10th Congressional against incumbent Scott Perry |url=https://local21news.com/news/local/janelle-stelson-concedes-in-race-for-10th-congressional-against-incumbent-scott-perry-congress-election-results-congressman-us-pa-pennsylvania |access-date=2026-03-24 |website=WHP |language=en}}</ref>

=== 2026 election ===
{{Main|2026 United States House of Representatives elections in Pennsylvania#District 10|l1 = 2026 Pennsylvania's 10th congressional district election}}
In July 2025, Stelson announced her candidacy for Pennsylvania's [[Pennsylvania's 10th congressional district|10th congressional district]] in the [[2026 United States House of Representatives elections in Pennsylvania#District 10|2026]] election.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Levy |first=Marc |date=2025-07-14 |title=The challenger who narrowly lost to Rep. Scott Perry wants another chance to beat him in 2026 |url=https://www.wtae.com/article/pennsylvania-perry-stelson-2026-house-race/65400106 |access-date=2025-12-04 |website=WTAE |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=FEC Form 2 for Report FEC-1900468 |url=https://docquery.fec.gov/cgi-bin/forms/H4PA10104/1900468/ |access-date=2025-12-04 |website=docquery.fec.gov}}</ref> The following month, she established residency and registered to vote at a rented home in [[Cumberland County, Pennsylvania|Cumberland County]] within the district;<ref>{{Cite news |last=Walters |first=Mark |date=August 20, 2025 |title=Janelle Stelson moves into 10th Congressional District, changing voter registration |url=https://www.ydr.com/story/news/politics/elections/2025/08/20/janelle-stelson-moved-into-the-district-as-she-gears-up-for-pa-10-race/85735631007/ |access-date=2026-03-24 |website=York Daily Record |language=en-US}}</ref> she also continued to own her former home in [[Lancaster County, Pennsylvania|Lancaster County]].<ref name="pnct">{{cite news |url=https://www.pennlive.com/politics/2025/08/janelle-stelson-can-now-vote-for-herself-for-congress-heres-why.html |title=Janelle Stelson can now vote for herself for Congress. Here's why |date=August 14, 2025 |website=[[PennLive]] |first=Charles |last=Thompson |access-date=April 27, 2026}}</ref> During the Democratic primary, her opponent, [[Dauphin County, Pennsylvania|Dauphin County]] Commissioner Justin Douglas, criticized her for declining to participate in a candidate debate, which marked the first Democratic primary for the district since 2016 not to have a debate.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Thompson |first1=Charles |title=Stelson frustrates opponent by skipping debates in primary for Pa.’s 10th House District |url=https://www.pennlive.com/politics/2026/05/stelson-frustrates-opponent-by-skipping-debates-in-primary-for-pas-10th-house-district.html |access-date=18 June 2026 |work=pennlive |date=6 May 2026 |language=en}}</ref> Stelson defeated Douglas in the Democratic primary with 67.5% of the vote, and advanced to a rematch against incumbent Republican Scott Perry in the general election.<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 25, 2026 |title=Pennsylvania Primary Election Results 2026 |url=https://apps.npr.org/primary-election-results-2026/states/PA.html |access-date=July 16, 2026 |website=NPR |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Levy |first=Marc |date=2026-05-19 |title=Shapiro-backed Democrats win House primaries in Pennsylvania swing districts the party hopes to flip |url=https://apnews.com/article/pennsylvania-primary-congress-governor-shapiro-garrity-8c19116119a331addf39ae97bc5149bf |access-date=2026-07-16 |website=AP News |language=en}}</ref>

Governor [[Josh Shapiro]] and Lieutenant Governor [[Austin Davis (politician)|Austin Davis]] both endorsed Stelson before the primary and the [[Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee|DCCC]] placed her into its "Red to Blue" program for its most competitive pick-up opportunities.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sweitzer |first=Justin |date=2026-05-20 |title=‘Game on’: Janelle Stelson advances to general election rematch against Scott Perry |url=https://www.cityandstatepa.com/politics/2026/05/game-janelle-stelson-advances-general-election-rematch-against-scott-perry/413655/ |access-date=2026-11-02 |website=City & State PA |language=en}}</ref> Stelson had raised more than $8.69 million to Perry's $6.45 million and outside groups had by then spent over $15 million on the campaign.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Panyard |first=Jack |date=2026-10-23 |title=Stelson holds cash advantage in closely watched race against Perry |url=https://www.witf.org/2026/10/22/stelson-holds-cash-advantage-in-closely-watched-race-against-perry/ |access-date=2026-11-02 |website=WITF |language=en}}</ref> 

== Political positions ==
Stelson supports updating immigration laws and has said that [[United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement|ICE]] should be held accountable for [[United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement#2026 killings of American citizens|the deaths of U.S. citizens]]. She is opposed to the [[2026 Iran War]], believing tax dollars would be better spent on domestic issues to help the middle class. She is also against [[Tariffs in the second Trump administration|tariffs enacted by President Trump]].<ref name="ydrma">{{cite news |url=https://www.ydr.com/story/news/politics/elections/2026/04/24/justin-douglas-challenges-janelle-stelson-in-primary-to-unseat-scott-perry/89723530007/ |title=Janelle Stelson faces progressive challenger in 10th District primary |date=April 24, 2026 |newspaper=[[York Daily Record]] |first=Mike |last=Argento |author-link=Mike Argento |access-date=April 27, 2026 |url-access=subscription}}</ref> Stelson criticized Perry for voting for the [[One Big Beautiful Bill Act]], citing its cuts to [[Medicaid]].<ref name="Sweitzer2026-1">{{Cite web |last=Sweitzer |first=Justin |date=2026-10-15 |title=PA-10 debate night: Scott Perry and Janelle Stelson spar over the economy, the Iran war and elections |url=https://www.cityandstatepa.com/politics/2026/10/pa-10-debate-night-scott-perry-and-janelle-stelson-spar-over-economy-iran-war-and-elections/416604/ |access-date=2026-11-02 |website=City & State PA |language=en}}</ref> She also called for giving [[Medicare (United States)|Medicare]] broader authority to negotiate prescription drug prices.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Knol |first=Katie |date=2026-10-06 |title=Election 2026: Where Scott Perry, Janelle Stelson stand on health care, safety |url=https://www.witf.org/2026/10/06/election-2026-where-scott-perry-janelle-stelson-stand-on-health-care-safety/ |access-date=2026-11-02 |website=WITF |language=en}}</ref> On data centers, she argued that developers should supply their own electricity rather than draw power from the existing grid.<ref name="Sweitzer2026-1" />

== Personal life ==
Stelson lives in [[East Pennsboro Township, Cumberland County, Pennsylvania|East Pennsboro Township]] in [[Cumberland County, Pennsylvania|Cumberland County]].<ref name="pnct" />
